chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Muskān, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, from a man, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
A woman does not undo her hair when she performs ghusl from janabah.

key_terms.اغْتَسَلَتْ: she performed ghusl; undertook the ritual bath
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: janabah; the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman; the subject of this legal ruling
key_terms.شَعْرَهَا: her hair; what is mentioned as not needing to be undone
key_terms.لَا تَنْقُضُ: she does not undo; indicates the absence of obligation

ai.seo_question: Does a woman have to undo her hair for ghusl from janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ghusl from janabah for women. It states that a woman is not required to undo her hair when performing the ritual bath, indicating facilitation in the laws of ritual purity.
